description: Audit a DMARC record. Reports an absent or unrecognised policy tag, which makes the whole record ignored; a pct below 100, where the policy applies to that share of failing mail and the rest is treated as none, so a rollout left part way is not the policy it appears to be; a subdomain policy weaker than the organisational one; a reporting address outside the domain, which needs an authorising record there or no reports arrive; and a tag DMARC does not define. Pay 180000 atomic USDC on Base via exact x402. MCP does not pay; it provides a challenge handoff.

domain.description: The domain, used to tell an internal reporting address from an external one. A trailing dot is ignored, so it does not create a second name.

record.description: The DMARC record, as published at _dmarc under the domain. Nothing resolves DNS: the records are supplied, which keeps the egress surface at zero and means an arbitrary domain can be audited without this service holding an allowlist for it.
record.example: v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; sp=none; pct=25; rua=mailto:dmarc@reports.vendor.test; adkim=s; ri=86400; policy=strict

require_reporting.description: Report an absent aggregate reporting address. Defaults to true, since without reports there is no way to know what a policy is doing before it is tightened.

name: dmarc_record_audit

complete.description: Whether everything supplied was examined. False means part of it was not, which is a different problem from something that is wrong.

finding_count.description: The true total, even when the listing is bounded.

passed.description: The same verdict under the name shared across the caller-supplied families.

request_id.description: Delivery request identifier; also returned in x-foundry-request-id.

tags.description: Every tag as published, so the reading is auditable.

valid.description: True only when the record parsed, every tag was recognised, and nothing was left unexamined.

title: DMARC Record Audit
